Vanessa / Priyom,

I've run a tax-entity lookup and validated the VAT IDs provided. Summary: Brightwell Ltd (GB 123456789) — UK VAT registered; Brightwell Ireland Ltd (IE IE9876543) — Irish VAT registered and valid. Given this, two practical options:

Option A (preferred): Issue two invoices linked by our reference (DL-2026-0487):
  - Invoice #1 to Brightwell Ltd (GB): hosting and any services physically supplied in UK — apply UK VAT where applicable.
  - Invoice #2 to Brightwell Ireland Ltd (IE): software/platform subscription lines treated as intra-EU B2B — reverse-charge (0% on our side, buyer accounts VAT).

Option B: Single invoice with split tax treatment on line items (requires clear legal entity/recipient for accounting). Some ERPs prefer two invoices; others accept one combined invoice with entity-level address blocks.

Evidence required to apply reverse charge to the Irish entity:
  - Copy of the Irish VAT registration (we've got this)
  - PO referencing the correct invoice recipient and VAT number
  - Contact name in finance for cross-checking at payment time

I've attached a draft split invoice layout for your review: Draft_Brightwell_SPLIT_INV_1102.pdf (draft). Key notes on the draft: we add a reference to the reverse charge article on the invoice footer and include the buyer VAT ID on each line.

Payments note: Priyom — if we issue two invoices, any chance we can coordinate settlement instructions so Brightwell can pay in a single transfer with remittance referencing both invoice numbers? That will cut lockbox/time-to-clear issues.

References: https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vat — we'll include the legal language we print on the invoice footer per EU guidance.
